description: Define MentorAgent Level-2 specialist agents in YAML instead of C#. Wraps the Agent Framework's declarative agent factory and plugs the resulting agents into MentorAgent's handoff graph, reusing the existing tools with their role checks and human-approval gates intact. Optional — install only if you want file-based agent definitions.
releaseNotes:
1.0.0-rc.1

		The first release candidate. No new features and no defects found in this package: the QA campaign closed 39 findings across the family and none of them was here. What changed is that the two properties this package exists to guarantee are now tests rather than claims.

		=== Now pinned by tests =====================================================
		- The scan reaches only where you pointed it. *.agent.yaml is the default pattern rather than *.yaml, because a deployment folder holds other YAML and reading a CI file as an agent definition would at best fail loudly. Recursion is off by default, because a nested folder is exactly where something gets dropped without review. Load order is stable (ordered by path), so two same-named agents cannot resolve differently between machines.
		- A tool named in YAML resolves to a tool the application already registered, already wrapped in MentorAgent's gate - so RequiredRoles, human approval, action feedback and per-tool metrics keep working inside a declarative agent's own function-calling loop. A definition file cannot grant itself a capability the application does not already have.
		- ConfigurationSection exposes that section and demonstrably nothing else. Null means "expose nothing", never "expose everything". This matters more than it looks: the Agent Framework's factory loads whatever configuration it is handed into the Power Fx engine as one variable per key, in its constructor, so a single key that is not a valid identifier takes the factory down before any definition is read. Never hand it the whole IConfiguration.
		- A missing directory warns (almost always a CopyToOutputDirectory miss - the assistant otherwise starts fine and is simply missing a specialist nobody thinks to look for), while no directory configured stays silent. Blank inline definitions are skipped rather than handed to the parser, since one empty string would otherwise lose every other definition in the same load.
		- A malformed or unloadable definition is logged and skipped; it never prevents the assistant from starting.

		=== Reminder ================================================================
		- A definition file is code. It chooses the model, writes the system instructions and names the callable tools. Load it only from deploy-time locations - never an upload folder, a user-writable path, or a path built from request input.

		=== Versions ================================================================
		- Microsoft.Agents.AI.Declarative stays pinned to the 1.6.1 line, matching Microsoft.Agents.AI in the core package. The head of that package is on a different Agent Framework version and taking it would drag the whole library along for a design-time convenience.
title: MentorAgent.Declarative
